name: Al Souika District
hero_subtitle: The oldest residential quarter, all blue-washed steps, carved doorways and quiet corners.

overview.title: The Blue Heart of the Old Town
overview.p1: Al Souika is one of the oldest residential areas in the medina, and where the town's famous blue looks its best. Narrow cobbled lanes wind up and down between blue-washed houses, with carved wooden doors, potted plants and small stairways at every turn.
overview.p2: There's no list of sights to tick off. The pleasure is getting a little lost. Go early, before the day trippers arrive, and keep in mind that these are people's homes. Keep your voice down, ask before photographing anyone and don't block doorways. The reward is a calm, beautiful walk.

moods.title: What to Look For in Al Souika
moods.subtitle: Details that make the walk.

1.title: Shades of Blue
1.desc: Look closely: walls range from pale sky to deep indigo, and no two lanes are quite alike.

2.title: Carved Doorways
2.desc: Wooden doors with studs and carving are a highlight. Photograph them without blocking the way.

3.title: Early Morning Calm
3.desc: Before the day-trippers arrive, the alleys feel almost private. Go early for the best atmosphere.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Al Souika District

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Enter from Place Outa el Hammam or Bab El Ain and let the alleys guide you uphill. A map app works, but getting lost is part of it.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Early morning is best for light and quiet. Midday and weekends are busier, and shops open later.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: These are private homes. Ask before photographing people, keep your voice low and wear shoes with grip for the steps.

q1.question: Why is Chefchaouen blue?
q1.answer: There are several theories: Jewish refugees in the 1930s, a natural mosquito repellent, and keeping homes cool.

q2.question: What is the best time to explore Al Souika?
q2.answer: Early morning, before 10 am, for soft light and quiet alleys.

q3.question: Is it OK to photograph people in the alleys?
q3.answer: Always ask first. Many locals prefer not to be photographed, and these are private homes.

q4.question: How long should I spend in the blue alleys?
q4.answer: One to three hours, depending on how much you like to wander and photograph.
